GRADE FOUR PRIMARY
 ENGLISH
 Essence Statement
English is:
• the major language of education, information, trade, diplomacy and social networking.
• an official language in Kenya but most importantly, the medium of instruction in our schools
 from Grade Four.
• key to the realisation of the National Goals of Education, the link to the global community and
 the door to the worldwide information network.
• so, the Kenyan education system should inculcate, in the learner, proficiency in English through
 the curriculum.

• ENHANCING LANGUAGE LEARNING THROUGH TECHNOLOGY
In the Upper Primary English Curriculum Design, there are four strands,
namely, listening and speaking, reading, grammar and writing. Each week,
English has been allocated four lessons. Hence, the curriculum is designed in
such a way that every week, the learner should be taken through an oral lesson,
a reading lesson, a grammar lesson and a writing lesson.
Progression of English Lessons during the week
Lesson one Listening and speaking
Lesson two Reading
Lesson three Grammar
Lesson four Writing
Although each lesson focuses on either listening and speaking, reading, grammar
writing, aspects of the other skills should be emphasised during the lesson.
 For example, the sounds and words introduced during the oral lesson could be
corporated into a reading passage.
 During the grammar lesson, learners could construct sentences using vocabulary
troduced in the comprehension passage.
 Learners could write compositions based on the theme or characters in the reading
ssage.
 Competency based language learning also requires the integration of pertinent and
ntemporary issues as well as values into the learning experiences.
